title: How can a missing number help us divide?
description: Twelve divided by four is turned into a multiplication with a missing number. Counting in fours until twelve is reached gives the missing number. Keeko raises the doubt of turning the numbers round.
teaching_notes: One idea: a division can be asked as a multiplication with a missing number. Watch for students who put the dividend and the divisor in the wrong places when they turn a division into a multiplication.

video_script.why: A learner sees that every division can be turned into a multiplication with a missing number, which is the idea used for dividing fractions.
video_script.substitution: the numbers of the book's own first division, twelve and four
video_script.anchor: twelve divided by four written beside four times a missing number equals twelve
video_script.wrong_move: turns the division round and asks twelve times what number is four
video_script.payoff_line: Twelve divided by four is three
maths_rules: 4, 8, 12 are the multiples of 4 up to 12
the slip: 12 × ? = 4 gives ? = 1/3, which answers a different question
video_script.design: A division and a multiplication with a missing number, joined by a double arrow. A count of fours runs below.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the division 12 ÷ 4 on the board

marks.pose: the division arrives on the board
marks.ask: a question mark glows beside the division

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about dividing.
<bookmark mark='pose'/>Find twelve divided by four, by asking what number times four gives twelve.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is twelve divided by four?

beats.on_screen: the division stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: 12 ÷ 4 = ? beside 4 × ? = 12, joined by a double arrow

marks.link: the division and the multiplication are joined by a double arrow
marks.ask: the missing number is marked with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='link'/>Every division can be turned into a multiplication with a missing number.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Twelve divided by four asks, four times what number is twelve?

marks.given: the two numbers are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers are twelve and four.

marks.find: the words To find and the division are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find twelve divided by four.

marks.write: the division is rewritten as a multiplication with a missing number

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step one, write the division as a multiplication with a missing number, four times what is twelve?

marks.count: jumps of four are drawn along a line from zero until twelve is reached

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step two, count in fours until we reach twelve, four, eight, twelve.

beats.on_screen: number of fours added to reach 12 = the missing number

marks.jumps: the jumps along the line are counted one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='jumps'/>Step three, count how many fours were added to reach twelve. That count is the missing number.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Twelve divided by four is three, because four times three is twelve.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 12 × ? = 4; the bubble is struck through and 4 × ? = 12 is written

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows twelve times a missing number equals four
marks.fix: four times a missing number equals twelve is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we ask twelve times what number is four, so the answer is one third.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>But that answers a different question, and it turns the division round.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>We divide by four, so it is four that gets multiplied by the missing number.
